also: this is not the place to

terms.grammar: noun, second declension; plural locī (single spots, passages) and loca (places, a region)
evidence: Cato Agr. 68: in suō quidque locō repōnitō
terms.comment: suō quidque locō, each thing in its place.

terms.gloss: situation, site (of a town, a house)
terms.comment: How a place lies; mostly of towns and land.

terms.gloss: on the spot, at the scene itself
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.250: in rem praesentem venīre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of being at the place itself; to go to the place to see for oneself is in rem praesentem venīre (Lewis & Short, s.v. praesum).

phrases.latin: omnia quīs ūsus erit, in suō quidque locō repōnitō
phrases.english: put everything you will need back, each thing in its own place

phrases.latin: et castra eō ipsō locō ubi pugnātum erat, imperātor Rōmānus posuit.
phrases.english: and the Roman commander pitched camp on the very spot where the battle had been fought.
